question: ___________ word of Indian dance is derived from a Sanskrit word and literally means ‘taking towards’.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Abhinaya**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Abhinaya** is derived from the Sanskrit word and literally means '**taking towards**'.
 
• It is an important aspect of Indian classical dance and involves the art of expression.
 
• Abhinaya encompasses the dramatic and expressive aspects of the dance, focusing on conveying emotions and storytelling.
 
• It is one of the four main components of Indian dance, the others being** Nritta (pure dance), Nritya (expressive dance), and Natya (dramatic dance)**.
 
• Abhinaya is crucial in making the performance more engaging and connecting with the audience on an emotional level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Indian classical dance has a rich history and is deeply rooted in the cultural and spiritual traditions of India.
 
• There are several classical dance forms in India, including Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, and Kathakali, each with its own unique style and technique.
 
• The Natya Shastra, an ancient Indian treatise on performing arts, is considered the foundational text for Indian classical dance and theatre.
 
• Abhinaya is detailed extensively in the Natya Shastra, outlining the various types of expressions (**Angika, Vachika, Aharya, and Sattvika**) used in performances.
 
• Mastery of Abhinaya requires rigorous training and practice, as it involves nuanced facial expressions, gestures, and body movements to effectively convey the intended emotions and narrative.
